description: University of Edinburgh's central AI innovation platform providing a secure gateway to multiple large language models, APIs, and locally-hosted options; guidance states data is not retained by third-party services to train models or for other purposes, though user chat histories are kept private to the user in ELM.
howToObtain: Access via the University ELM portal using university credentials; March 2026 guidance describes ELM as free to all staff and students, while another published entitlement page states discretionary School approval, an administrative condition whose universal applicability remains unestablished.
costToUser: Free to all staff and students (qualification gap applies).

evidence.evidenceSnippet: All University of Edinburgh students have free access to ELM (Edinburgh access to Language Models), which offers you a secure gateway to a range of generative AI models.
keeps your chat histories and document downloads private to you in ELM, and is free to all staff and students.
Current staff and students are entitled to use ELM subject to discretionary School approval.

The university encourages you to use ELM over other platforms such as GPT, DeepSeek, Grok etc for the following reasons:
In ELM your data is secure – it will not be retained by third party services to train their models or for any other purpose.
It is free to use for all staff and students, providing the same access for all and saving you money.

description: Locally-hosted instance of Llama in ELM featuring optimized architecture for faster response times and reduced power consumption.
howToObtain: Select Llama model within the ELM platform.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: ELM provides access to a range of language models including a locally-hosted instance of Llama. This has an optimized architecture that can achieve faster response times and reduced power consumption.

description: Microsoft Copilot chat service integrated into Edge browser with enterprise data protection when signed in with University of Edinburgh credentials.
howToObtain: Sign in to Microsoft Edge browser using University of Edinburgh credentials; verified by a green shield icon.

evidence.evidenceSnippet: Copilot chat service within Edge - you can access this by signing into the Microsoft Edge browser with your University credentials. A green shield will appear, giving you additional protections: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/microsoft-365/enterprise-data-protection

description: Full Microsoft 365 Copilot product integrated with Office applications (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel) for automated drafting and meeting summaries.
howToObtain: Not available via University of Edinburgh institutional licensing agreement.

evidence.evidenceSnippet:
Copilot integration with our MS365 services is part of a larger Microsoft 'Copilot for MS365' product that we do not currently have available in our service provision and our licence agreement with Microsoft.
ISG currently do not have any plans to make the full Copilot for MS365 license available at this time.
